title: SOP for Cnidaria - Anthozoa Specimen Collection, Processing, and Preservation
author: Melanie Van Weddingen

steps.title: Identify specimens and record data
steps.instruction: After collection (by hand, dredge, trawl, or brushing), keep specimens in ambient seawater containers. Record sampling date, station number, GPS coordinates, sampling method, harvesters, and habitat on a field sheet. Complete a tracking sheet with taxon name (species, genus, rank), taxonomist name, and sex. For large Scleractinia colonies, sample by hand and collect only a small piece to avoid habitat damage. Process soft coral quickly after dredging or trawling. Ensure CITES permits are obtained for protected Anthozoa species.

steps.title: Photograph specimens for voucher
steps.instruction: Using a macro lens, capture the highest‑resolution images of each specimen in a clean glass container filled with seawater; change the water between specimens. Take a reference photo that includes a ruler, the batch QR code (e.g., 1 ATLASea), the specimen barcode (e.g., 1 MNHN‑IK), the tracking sheet, and the station label. Then take a general photo, gently shake the coral if needed to extend tentacles, and capture close‑up photos of tentacles, surface patterns, and polyps (for colonies). Discuss photograph requirements with the taxonomist; photographs serve as a voucher when a physical voucher cannot be retained.

steps.title: Dissect and flash‑freeze tissue pieces
steps.instruction: While the specimen is still alive, for colonial taxa sample an individual colony. Remove all visible contaminants and epibionts (including any substrate) by washing and gently brushing in filtered seawater (FSW); gut contents and symbionts may remain. Blot to remove excess seawater and mucus. Dissect the tissue into 15 pieces of approximately 300–500 mg each. For soft tissues aim for ~300 mg per tube; for hard tissues (e.g., polyps with skeleton) aim for 500–1000 mg per tube. Cut each piece into smaller fragments, place each fragment in a uniquely labeled tube, and flash‑freeze the tubes in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Preserve tissue pieces in ethanol
steps.instruction: Dissect an additional 10 pieces of approximately 500 mg each and place each piece in a tube containing 98 % ethanol. Store the tubes at –20 °C. After ethanol addition, weight each tube and scan its barcode onto the log sheet.

steps.title: Store voucher at MNHN
steps.instruction: Retain the leftover organism material (as many hard parts/tissues as possible or another individual from the same population verified by a taxonomist). Place the MNHN‑IK barcode and the station label on the tube or container. Add 85 % ethanol so that the ethanol volume is at least ten times the specimen volume. Seal the container and ship the voucher to MNHN according to SOP‑0 general instructions.
